whatThisCheckpointIsFor: OPS-25 D-14's dispatch: 'CP2: D-14 done, with its hash read back.' D-14 is the only row this checkpoint grades. D-13's parcels are graded in the close.
verdict: D-14 PASS on all five of the row's steps

ciConclusionsReadPerJobAsTheDispatchRequ.job: Gitleaks — detect secrets in code and history

step1_landTheHealthcheckFixOnMain.noteOnWhyPerJobMatters: read per job against the current base rather than as one roll-up string, per the dispatch; all three jobs are scanner checks, so the fix was gated by supply-chain and secret scanning and by nothing that would have caught a wrong healthcheck
step1_landTheHealthcheckFixOnMain.whatTheFixIs: Dockerfile.api's HEALTHCHECK called `curl`, which node:22-slim does not ship, so the probe failed on every attempt and DigitalOcean reported a correctly-working service as unhealthy. The fix replaces it with node's global fetch and raises start-period 40s -> 120s.
step1_landTheHealthcheckFixOnMain.contradictionChecked: the dispatcher's own premise that the fix was 'on the pin branch and not on main' was re-measured at CP1 rather than taken on report: origin/main lacked exactly one file against the pin, Dockerfile.api.

whatTheProofEstablished: main BUILDS: the app reached ACTIVE having built the API image from main's own Dockerfile.api
main STARTS: /api/health answers 200 with db:connected, so the process comes up against a real database
main SERVES: the platform routes answer, and all nine comparable feeds return the same records it returns in production (measured in the close's per-feed matrix)

whatTheProofWasShapedLikeAndWhy.envsWereBuiltFromGcpSecretManager: P:/seat-worktrees/d14-d13-v1-reach/_build-proof-spec.mjs read the smartcity-os-prod secret values and composed the spec, so the proof app's environment matches production's rather than a convenient subset. A first attempt with a placeholder environment failed on VFD_JWT_SECRET, which is the failure mode this avoids.
whatTheProofWasShapedLikeAndWhy.whyThatMatters: a proof app with a thin environment would have 'proved' a build while proving nothing about the startup path, and the row's step 2 exists specifically because main also carries the D-10 scraper commit, which touches only scraper files, so whether the API image is unaffected is a question to establish and not to assume

step2_proveMainOnANonProductionApp.removalCarried: the app was removed by this lane after its commit was read back; the removal and its timestamp are recorded in the close. The spec is reproducible from _build-proof-spec.mjs, so the removal costs re-verifiability nothing but a script run.

step3_repointWalrusAppAtMain.verdict: PASS — read back byte for byte
step3_repointWalrusAppAtMain.readFromWhere: the ACTIVE deployment object's services[0].source_commit_hash, read through the DigitalOcean API (apps/{id}/deployments, phase ACTIVE), not from the spec's declared branch
step3_repointWalrusAppAtMain.whyThatDistinctionIsThePoint: the spec's branch is an intention; source_commit_hash is what the container is running. Rule 13 exists because these two disagreed once and the deploy still reported SUCCESS.
step3_repointWalrusAppAtMain.intermediateDeploymentsObserved: e243db0a-b5ed-4f4c-bb8c-74261ab97b2d (ACTIVE, 1f0262f1); before it e32caf51 (SUPERSEDED, e783f351) — so the read-back names a real transition from the pin to main and not a steady state that happened to match

step4_externalPayloadComparison.verdict: PASS — 0 unexplained changes on both public hostnames
step4_externalPayloadComparison.vantage: GCP Cloud Build, project smartcity-os-prod (OPS-25 rule 10); credential sent: none. Rule 11 applies: payload compared by normalized SHA-256, framing ignored.

theFourChangedByDesign.whyThisIsTheRepointWorkingAndNotARegress: these are G-159's four platform finance routes. On the pin they did not exist, so the request fell through to the SPA shell. On main they exist and refuse a keyless caller. A change from 'no such route' to 'route exists, refuses you' is exactly what the repoint was for.

step4_externalPayloadComparison.theIdenticalSixteenInclude: the health endpoint, the SPA shell, an unknown /api/platform/* path as a negative control, all five MyGov routes, Samsara, Spireon, FirstDue, Power BI, GoTo and both property-intel routes — each unchanged in status, body kind and byte count
step4_externalPayloadComparison.unexplainedChangeRule: any path whose payload moved for a reason not on the G-159 list would have been printed as UNEXPLAINED and would have stopped this checkpoint; the count is 0

g159RoutesPresentFromOutsideWithoutAKey.verdict: PASS — the recorded tell reproduces exactly
g159RoutesPresentFromOutsideWithoutAKey.tell: a route that exists answers 401 JSON; an unknown /api/platform/* path answers the SPA shell with 200

unknownPathControl.reading: the SPA shell, i.e. the route does not exist — which is what makes the four 401s mean 'exists and refuses' rather than 'everything 401s'

deployOnPushDisabled.measured: services[0].github.deploy_on_push is absent (null) on walrus-app, d14-main-proof, d12-main-uat and dolphin-app
deployOnPushDisabled.consequence: a merge to main ships nothing; every ship in this lane is a deliberate act with source_commit_hash read back

gcpSmartcityApiUntouched.howItIsEstablished: by the absence of any write: no mutation was issued to any GCP resource by this lane, and the host's only role here was as the comparison target in the per-feed probe. It still answers its own named 503 refusals and still serves G-159's routes as absent, which is the pre-repoint state it is kept for (rule 3).
gcpSmartcityApiUntouched.whyTheAbsenceOfAWriteIsTheRightInstrumen: rule 3 asks that the rollback copy not be modified, so the measurement that matters is that it was not, and no positive state of a never-written resource can show that better than the absence of the write

leaveBehind: None. The one thing this lane created, the d14-main-proof DigitalOcean app, was removed after its commit was read back, so nothing is left running. The three apps this lane mutated (walrus-app, d12-main-uat) are the row's own subjects, not residue.
